content:
Comprising what was once southeastern Appalachian Ohio, Burning Springs was greatly affected by a phenomenon known as the Rust in the aftermath of the Great War, causing significant environmental damage[1] and giving the area a desert-like appearance.[2] Chemical spills from Abraxodyne Chemical, a company that had a significant presence in the region before the bombs, caused the Rust,[3] affecting many of its residents with a serious illness. Prominent symptoms include heavy coughing and thirst.[4]

Immediately after the war, members of the Ohio National Guard initially attempted to keep order in Athens while the Rust took its toll on the area, with sick individuals dying and being disposed of in burn pits,[5] and seismic activity in the aftermath of the bombs caused further damage to the city.[6] All the while, bandits began skulking the roads outside the city,[7] and National Guardsmen realized they were not receiving reinforcements any time soon, with communication lines severed.[8] As much of the civilian population dwindled, either by death or fleeing the area, the National Guardsmen became affected by the Rust as well, and were forced to abandon the city as the nightmarish situation in Athens became "untenable."[8][9]

At some point, an Enclave transport vertibird carrying a sedated super mutant crashed south of Athens and he escaped their custody.[10] Possessing unusual intelligence while still having a hefty bloodlust, this super mutant became known as the Rust King, who sought to conquer the area. He formed the Rust King's Army, his followers being composed of violent raiders, and they established the Rust Kingdom in an old Abraxodyne facility.[11] The Rust King's forces went on to conquer Fort Steuben and construct Checkpoint Canyon, establishing dominance over the region.[12][13]

Burning Springs is the second region of Appalachia (following Skyline Valley) that was not present in-game at release; it was introduced with a westward map expansion as part of the Burning Springs update.

Burning Springs has an invisible barrier along the Ohio River that extends into the eastern edges of the region itself, dividing the region and the Forest. Because of this, the only way to currently travel between the two regions without fast travel is using or going directly around the Silver Bridge within Point Pleasant. According to developers, this barrier will eventually be removed, but it is currently reserved for future plans.[Non-game 1]

Overall, the Burning Springs region is a segment of the real-world area known as Appalachian Ohio. According to producer Bill LaCoste, the real-world range of Burning Springs could be compared to "south of Point Pleasant/Gallipolis, west to about Dexter [City] maybe, and up north to Athens. So just a really small SE portion of it."[Non-game 2]

There are several parts of the Burning Springs region that are inaccessible, but were visibly adjusted on the world map to accommodate for the new region. Producer Rebeccah Bassell did not confirm nor deny that these areas were being saved for future content, but did mention that it was easier for the development team to "add space" into the map rather than take away from or restrict existing lands, especially in the context of player C.A.M.P. placement. Rebeccah said that the borders of Burning Springs seen in the Public Test Server were the intended borders to launch with for the live release of the Burning Springs update, but also said "the wasteland has a way of always changing."[Non-game 1] When asked about boarded-up buildings at locations in Burning Springs, Rebeccah said "[we] will be holding off opening more locations for reasons or maybe not reasons but it's on our radar!"[Non-game 3]The Rust King also hints toward future story content in dialogue at the end of When the Rust Settles,[14] and Bethesda Game Studios have confirmed Burning Springs is only the first entry in a story spanning multiple chapters and updates.[Non-game 4]

References[]

↑Vault 76 dweller: "What do you know about the Rust?" Pop: "What does anyone know? It's death itself. It came after the Bombs, and took all the plants with it. I heard things started growing back in other places, but never here. Folks treat it like some kind of force of nature, but if you ask me? It ain't nature, it's us." (Pop's dialogue)

↑Vault 76 dweller: "What can you tell me about the area?" The Ghoul: "Ohio? Didn't think much of it before the bombs dropped, and it hasn't improved since. Never expected a desert out this way, though. Somebody really fucked it up." (The Ghoul's dialogue)

↑ 1.01.1Rebeccah Bassell on the Bethesda Game Studios official Discord: "The borders you're seeing around the map are the borders we're intending to launch with. Some inside baseball as to why: it's MUCH easier for us to add space to the map than to take it away/restrict for new content. The last thing we want to do is have someone build a cool CAMP somewhere and then bulldoze it when we release more things. Maybe we release more things there? Maybe we don't? Maybe I am a figment of your imagination? :hehe: TL;DR - yes, but stay tuned ❤️ The wasteland has a way of always changing!"
